title: PHYD57 Project Ideas: High-Performance Scientific Computing & HPC Architecture
text:
Every project proposed below meets five mandatory criteria designed to build deep, enduring expertise in the age of generative AI:

Semester Feasibility: Tailored to be independently architected, compiled, profiled, and benchmarked within a 12-week academic term by an individual student (or pair for the A4 capstone).
Curricular Grounding: Deeply integrated with the PHYD57 syllabus taught by Prof. Pawel Artymowicz—specifically applying compiler optimization flags (gcc, clang, nvcc), OpenMP multi-threading, microprocessor cache architecture, SIMD vectorization (AVX2/AVX-512), CUDA GPU kernels, Barnes-Hut octree algorithms, or Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH).
AI Automation Resilience: Focuses on hardware-aware systems programming where statistical AI is notoriously incapable: eliminating thread divergence in GPU warp scheduling, avoiding false sharing in CPU L1/L2 cache lines, maximizing hardware memory coalescing, managing NUMA node memory affinity, and profiling against hardware Roofline models.
Academic Leverage (Impressing Faculty): Formulated to demonstrate the computational rigor that professors in computational physics and computer science look for—producing verified scaling curves, FLOP rate benchmarks, and clean reproducible C++/CUDA repositories.
Industry & Professional Value: Imparts direct, high-salary engineering capabilities required in high-performance computing (HPC), quantitative trading (low-latency C++ / FPGA / GPU execution), GPU kernel engineering (NVIDIA, AMD, Apple), aerospace simulation, and modern AI systems infrastructure.

title: PHYD57 Project Ideas: High-Performance Scientific Computing & HPC Architecture
section: 🚀 Project Option 1: GPU-Accelerated 3D Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with CUDA Shared Memory Tiling
text:
🚀 Project Option 1: GPU-Accelerated 3D Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with CUDA Shared Memory Tiling

1. Context & Motivation (PHYD57 Lectures 8–11)
Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) is a Lagrangian fluid simulation technique where continuous fluid fields (density \(\rho\), velocity \(\mathbf{v}\), pressure \(P\)) are approximated by interpolation over moving particles using a smoothing kernel \(W(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}', h)\): \[\rho_i = \sum_{j} m_j W(\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j, h)\] \[\frac{d\mathbf{v}_i}{dt} = -\sum_{j} m_j \left( \frac{P_i}{\rho_i^2} + \frac{P_j}{\rho_j^2} + \Pi_{ij} \right) \nabla_i W_{ij} + \mathbf{g}\] where \(\Pi_{ij}\) is the Monaghan artificial viscosity term preventing unphysical interparticle penetration.
On CPUs, neighbor searching dominates computation time (\(O(N^2)\) without spatial sorting). On GPUs, naive particle interactions suffer from uncoalesced global memory transactions and high warp divergence.


2. Concrete Deliverables & Scope

Parallel Spatial Hash Grid: Implement a 3D uniform spatial hash grid in CUDA. Use parallel radix sort (thrust::sort_by_key or custom CUDA kernel) on spatial cell IDs so neighbor particles occupy contiguous GPU global memory addresses.
Shared Memory Tiling Kernel: Write custom CUDA kernels for density and force computation that load cell neighbor particles into high-speed GPU shared memory (\(L1\) cache speed), eliminating redundant global memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
Tait Equation of State: Implement the weakly compressible Tait EOS: \[P(\rho) = B \left[ \left(\frac{\rho}{\rho_0}\right)^\gamma - 1 \right]\] with numerical speed of sound chosen to limit density fluctuations to \(< 1\%\).
Physics Benchmark: Simulate the 3D Rayleigh-Taylor instability or a breaking dam obstacle impact for \(N = 2 \times 10^5\) particles in real time.
Hardware Profiling: Use NVIDIA Nsight Compute to measure achieved memory bandwidth (GB/s), warp execution efficiency (\(> 85\%\)), and speedup relative to a multi-threaded OpenMP CPU baseline.



3. Why This Impresses Professors & Employers

Demonstrates mastery of low-level GPU hardware architecture: coalescing, bank conflicts in shared memory, and occupancy optimization.
Highly coveted skillset in game engine physics (Unreal Engine Niagara), visual effects (ILM, Weta), aerospace CFD, and GPU compiler engineering at tech firms.

title: PHYD57 Project Ideas: High-Performance Scientific Computing & HPC Architecture
section: ⚡ Project Option 2: AVX-512 SIMD Vectorized & OpenMP-Parallelized Barnes-Hut Octree Gravitational Engine
text:
⚡ Project Option 2: AVX-512 SIMD Vectorized & OpenMP-Parallelized Barnes-Hut Octree Gravitational Engine

1. Context & Motivation (PHYD57 Lectures 5–9)
Simulating gravitational interactions between \(N\) bodies by direct pairwise summation requires \(O(N^2)\) operations, becoming computationally intractable for \(N > 10^5\). The Barnes-Hut algorithm reduces complexity to \(O(N \log N)\) by grouping distant particles into an octree.
If a tree node of size \(s\) is at distance \(d\) from a particle such that the opening angle satisfies: \[\theta = \frac{s}{d} < \theta_{\text{crit}} \approx 0.7\] the entire sub-cluster is approximated by its center-of-mass multipole moment.
However, tree traversal involves irregular pointer chasing that thrashes the CPU cache hierarchy. Modern CPUs (Intel Xeon, AMD EPYC, modern Ryzen) achieve peak performance only when operations are vectorized across 256-bit (AVX2) or 512-bit (AVX-512) SIMD registers.


2. Concrete Deliverables & Scope

Cache-Conscious Linear Octree: Implement a Morton-indexed (Z-order curve) linear octree in C++ that stores node data in contiguous flat arrays rather than heap-allocated pointers, maximizing L1/L2 cache hit rates.
AVX-512 Explicit SIMD Intrinsics: Write hand-vectorized interaction kernels using Intel AVX2/AVX-512 intrinsics (_mm256_fmadd_ps / _mm512_fmadd_ps) that process 8 to 16 particle interactions simultaneously per vector register.
OpenMP Dynamic Work Stealing: Parallelize tree traversal using OpenMP tasking (#pragma omp task) with dynamic load balancing across CPU cores, preventing thread starvation when particles cluster non-uniformly.
Roofline Model & Hardware Performance Counters: Profile execution with Linux perf or Intel VTune. Construct an empirical Roofline Model plotting operational intensity (FLOP/byte) against memory bandwidth to prove the kernel operates near the hardware compute ceiling.



3. Why This Impresses Professors & Employers

Writing explicit SIMD intrinsics and cache-oblivious data structures demonstrates low-level systems programming that generic AI tools cannot generate reliably.
Direct relevance to high-frequency trading (low-latency order books, market data decoding), physics engines, and high-performance computing centers (Compute Canada / Digital Research Alliance).

title: PHYD57 Project Ideas: High-Performance Scientific Computing & HPC Architecture
section: 🌌 Project Option 3: Distributed Hybrid MPI + OpenMP Cosmological Particle-Mesh (PM) Spectral Gravitational Simulator
text:
🌌 Project Option 3: Distributed Hybrid MPI + OpenMP Cosmological Particle-Mesh (PM) Spectral Gravitational Simulator

1. Context & Motivation (PHYD57 Lectures 10–12)
On cosmological scales, the universe’s large-scale structure (filaments, clusters, and cosmic voids) evolves under self-gravity in an expanding Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) spacetime. The Particle-Mesh (PM) algorithm solves Poisson’s equation \(\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G a^2 \bar{\rho} \delta\) using Fast Fourier Transforms (FFTs) on a regular spatial grid: \[\tilde{\Phi}(\mathbf{k}) = -4\pi G a^2 \bar{\rho} \frac{\tilde{\delta}(\mathbf{k})}{k^2}\] achieving linear complexity \(O(N_g \log N_g)\) where \(N_g\) is the grid size.


2. Concrete Deliverables & Scope

Cloud-in-Cell (CIC) Density & Force Interpolation: Implement 3D Cloud-in-Cell trilinear mass assignment and force interpolation between continuous particles and discrete grid nodes.
FFTW 3D Spectral Poisson Solver: Use the FFTW3 library to compute exact spatial gradients via spectral multiplication in Fourier space (\(\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{k}) = -i \mathbf{k} \tilde{\Phi}(\mathbf{k})\)).
Expanding Universe Time Stepping: Implement a cosmological leapfrog symplectic integrator in conformal time or scale factor \(a(t)\), incorporating Hubble drag: \[\frac{d\mathbf{x}}{dt} = \frac{\mathbf{p}}{m a^2}, \quad \frac{d\mathbf{p}}{dt} = -\frac{1}{a} \nabla \Phi\]
Hybrid Parallelization (MPI + OpenMP): Implement 1D or 2D domain decomposition using MPI across distributed nodes and OpenMP threading within each node.
Cosmological Statistics: From the simulated structure at redshift \(z = 0\), compute the matter power spectrum \(P(k)\) and two-point correlation function \(\xi(r)\), benchmarking against analytical linear perturbation theory (Harrison-Zeldovich spectrum).



3. Why This Impresses Professors & Employers

Mastering distributed memory parallel computing (MPI) is the cornerstone requirement for supercomputing research (e.g. at CITA, Perimeter Institute, national laboratories).
Demonstrates complete full-stack computational physics competence: cosmological theory, spectral Fourier numerical methods, and distributed cluster scaling.
